title: Multipolar trap: capability race without coordination
summary: Every lab, government and company makes a locally rational choice: if we slow down, a competitor will not. Each choice raises the pressure on the others, and the collective result is capability racing ahead of safety and governance. Individual virtue cannot beat these incentives; only a coordination architecture that makes cooperation rational for every actor can.
source: Ch01 — Schmachtenberger, the multipolar trap (replaces the Burning Man figure)

nodes.label: Competitive Pressure
nodes.description: Fear that a rival will deploy, regulate or capture the market first

nodes.label: Locally Rational Choice
nodes.description: Each actor skips safety or governance to keep pace

nodes.label: Catastrophe Corridor
nodes.description: Gap between exponential capability and linear governance

nodes.label: Capability Race
nodes.description: Capabilities advancing as fast as incentives push them

nodes.label: Coordination Architecture
nodes.description: Systems that make cooperation the rational choice for every actor

edges.description: Pressure makes defecting from safety the rational local move
Every local choice speeds up the race
A faster race raises everyone else's pressure
Capability outruns safety, governance and coordination
A coordination architecture removes the incentive to defect
It would keep capability inside what governance can handle

identifiability_note: The coordination architecture (n5) has never been observed at civilizational scale. NOTE for the author: the text states the trap and its result; the loop closure (race raises pressure) is the standard reading of 'Nobody chose it. Everybody's in it.' and may want one sentence to anchor it.
